findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...). A team member is normally either an admin or an owner, not both, so legitimate team admins and owners will almost always fail this check and receive FORBIDDEN unless they also happen to be the organizer or an attendee. The condition should be a logical OR.

findings.title: Calendar is updated with the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The handler loads credentials for ctx.user and constructs EventManager from ctx.user, then calls updateCalendarAttendees for a booking owned by booking.user. When the caller is an attendee or a team admin/owner, this uses the wrong account's calendar credentials (or none at all), so the organizer's calendar event is not updated even though attendees are added in the database and notification emails are sent. It should use the booking organizer's user and credentials, as the booking query already loads booking.user.credentials.

findings.title: Guest de-duplication and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and do not deduplicate the input
findings.body: uniqueGuests compares guest === attendee.email exactly and checks blacklistedGuestEmails (which were lowercased) against the raw guest string. 'Guest@Example.com' therefore bypasses both the existing-attendee check and the blacklist, and because the server schema has no uniqueness refinement, the same address repeated in one guests array is inserted multiple times via createMany, producing duplicate Attendee rows. Emails should be normalized (trim/lowercase) and the input deduplicated server-side.

findings.title: Guests array is unbounded, enabling bulk attendee/email abuse
findings.body: ZAddGuestsInputSchema accepts an array of arbitrary length. Any organizer, attendee, or (intended) team admin can submit thousands of arbitrary email addresses in one call, creating thousands of Attendee rows, one calendar update, and a scheduled/invitation email to every address — effectively using Cal.com's mail infrastructure to spam third parties and inflating the booking. Add a reasonable .min(1).max(...) bound (and reject empty strings) in the server schema.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or past bookings
findings.body: After the NOT_FOUND check the handler never inspects booking.status or booking.endTime. addGuests will happily insert attendees, call updateCalendarAttendees, and send 'guests added'/scheduled emails for a cancelled, rejected, or already-ended event, resurrecting notifications and calendar invites for a dead booking. The handler should reject non-ACCEPTED (and past) bookings; note the UI also exposes the action for past confirmed bookings.

findings.title: Emails are sent using the unfiltered guests list instead of uniqueGuests
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) is passed the raw input rather than uniqueGuests. In sendAddGuestsEmails, attendees whose email is in that list receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notice, so pre-existing attendees who were filtered out of the insert (already on the booking) still get re-sent a fresh scheduled invitation, and case-mismatched addresses are misclassified. Pass uniqueGuests (normalized) instead.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type metadata
findings.body: Unlike sendLocationChangeEmails/sendScheduledEmails, which check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, team members, and every attendee, and the handler does not even pass the event type metadata. Event types configured with disableStandardEmails (e.g. for workflow-only notifications) will leak standard 'guests added' and scheduled emails. Thread the metadata through and honor the host/attendee disable flags.

findings.title: Stale validation error survives a successful submission
findings.body: onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never calls setIsInvalidEmail(false); the Cancel button does reset it. If a user first submits an invalid/duplicate email (setting isInvalidEmail), corrects it, and succeeds, the 'Emails must be unique and valid' error is still shown the next time the dialog opens for any booking. Reset isInvalidEmail in onSuccess (and on dialog close via onOpenChange, which currently also leaves both the emails and the error in place when dismissing with the X/backdrop).
